utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-03-66-R77, the Prosecutor of the Tribunal against Beqa Beqaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning. First of all, Mr. Beqaj, can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Beqaj. May I have the appearances. Prosecution first, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: May it please Your Honour, my name is Mr. Cayley, I appear on behalf of the Prosecutor with my colleague Mr. Colin Black and our case manager, Mr. Hasan Younis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cayley. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: May it please Your Honour, I appear on behalf of Mr. Beqaj. My name is Rodney Dixon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dixon. Mr. Beqaj, the purpose of this hearing is that you will have an opportunity to be confronted with the indictment brought against you and that the charges will be read to you and that you can enter a plea either today or within the next 30 days, and for that reason I, first of all, have to establish whether you are assisted by counsel. It least seems that you are. Have you had an opportunity to speak with Mr. Dixon?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did have the chance to talk to him. In Prstina I did have my own lawyer as well called Azem Vllasi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But Mr. Vllasi is not your counsel in these proceedings as far as I understand it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank Defence lawyer who is here present.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can confirm that I did have an opportunity on Friday to speak to Mr. Beqaj at some length about the proceedings and was able to advise him as far as we have material at this stage, and he is in a position today to proceed with the arraignment. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I also do understand that you are assigned for the initial appearance by the Registrar, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Yes. That is correct, Your Honour, as duty counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that Mr. Vllasi does not represent at this moment in these proceedings Mr. Beqaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Beqaj, please be seated. You may remain seated unless you really would prefer to stand. Did you receive a copy of the indictment, Mr. Beqaj?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have not received a copy of the indictment yet? Has Mr. Dixon received a copy of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I have received a copy of the indictment and have explained the indictment to Mr. Beqaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: And I believe that he was done upon his arrest as well. So there's no issue over that at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But is there already a copy of the indictment in a language Mr. Beqaj understands?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: I don't think there is. My learned friend may be able to assist. There is consultation going on at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is a copy in Albanian. I have it here. I'm not certain whether Mr. Dixon has it. It actually dates from the 29th of October. So it should have been severed on the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know whether the -- is that a translation was not available yet on the 29th?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: No. There is a translation. It's -- well, it's dated the 29th of October, so it must have been available on that date, the translation into Albanian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I'm a bit surprised that no such copy was given to the -- to the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I mean, I'm surprised, too, but I think it's actually the Registry's responsibility to do that, not the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is there a copy available for the Defence at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: We can certainly give them this copy, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Beqaj, there is now a copy in Albanian available of the -- of the indictment. I'd like to see it, perhaps, first. Yes. Yes. Mr. Beqaj, if you would like to take time to read the indictment in your own language, I'll give you that time. If you say, "I'm sufficiently aware of the charges on the basis of the conversation I had with counsel," then please tell me so that I know how to proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have been given the indictment in Pristina, and I am aware of it. I have read it, so I'm generally satisfied that I know what it is about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Apart from that, the indictment will be read to you anyhow during this meeting. We'll then proceed. Well, you say that you know what it is about. I take that as what would have been an answer to my next question is that whether you understand the indictment. I'd like the indictment against you, which is not a very long indictment, to be read out by the registrar. Madam Registrar, may I invite you to read out indictment in full.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The Prosecutor of the Tribunal against Beqa Beqaj. Indictment. The Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia, pursuant to her authority under Article 18 of the Statute of the International Criminal Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia and Rule 77 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the International Criminal Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia charges: Beqa Beqaj with contempt of the Tribunal, attempted content of the Tribunal, and incitement to contempt of the Tribunal. The accused, Beqa Beqaj, father's name Zecir, was born on 10th of November, 1952 in Petrove, Kosovo. He is a relative of Isak Musliu, an accused in the case of Prosecutor versus Fatmir Limaj, Haradin Bala, and Isak Musliu, case number IT-03-66. Charges: Counts 1 to 3, contempt, attempted contempt, and incitement to contempt of the Tribunal. From on or about 17 February 2003 through to on or about 19th of October, 2004, Beqa Beqaj, individually and in concert with others incited, attempted to commit, committed, or otherwise aided and abetted the commission of contempt of the Tribunal. During the time period set forth above, Beqa Beqaj knowingly and wilfully interfered with the administration of justice by threatening, intimidating, offering a bribe to, or otherwise interfering with witnesses or potential witnesses in the case of Prosecutor versus Limaj, Bala, and Musliu, case number IT-03-66. On or about 11th of June, 2004, in Shtime, Kosovo, the son of Beqa Beqaj accosted (redacted), a potential witness, blaming (redacted)for Isak Musliu's detention in The Hague. After this incident, on the same day, Beqa Beqaj told (redacted)that Isak Musliu had previously communicated from The Hague that Beqa Beqaj should go to (redacted)and demand him to withdraw his statement against Isak Musliu. In early September 2004, Beqa Beqaj contacted (redacted), a potential witness living outside of Kosovo, through a relative of (redacted) (redacted). The relative informed (redacted)that Beqa Beqaj had received calls directly from Isak Musliu in The Hague, and that Isak Musliu told Beqa Beqaj to tell (redacted)that he must withdraw his statement to the Tribunal. It was also suggested that Isak Musliu would reward (redacted) (redacted)with a gift of lands with (redacted)withdrew his statement. On or shortly before 27 September 2004, Beqa Beqaj again asked the relative to contact (redacted). The relative told (redacted)that Beqa Beqaj claimed to speak on behalf of Fatmir Limaj and Isak Musliu that (redacted)must travel back to Kosovo to meet with Defence lawyers and withdraw his statement. On or about 6 October 2004, Beqa Beqaj asked (redacted)by telephone to return to Kosovo meet with Fatmir Limaj's brother, Demir Limaj and a lawyer, in order to withdraw his statement against Isak Musliu and Fatmir Limaj and state that he had nothing to do with Musliu and Limaj. Beqa Beqaj told (redacted)that he had spoken with and acted on behalf of Isak Musliu, Fatmir Limaj, and Demir Limaj. On or about 13 October 2004, Beqa Beqaj again asked (redacted) by telephone to return to Kosovo meet with Demir Limaj or a lawyer in order to withdraw his statement against Isak Musliu and Fatmir Limaj and state that he knows nothing about Musliu and Limaj. By his acts and commissions, and omissions, Beqa Beqaj participated in: Count 1: Contempt of the Tribunal, punishable under this Tribunal's inherent power and Rule 77(A)(iv) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal; Count 2: Attempted contempt of the Tribunal, punishable under this Tribunal's inherent power and Rule 77(A)(iv) and Rule 77(B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal; or Count 3: Incitement to contempt of the Tribunal, punishable under this Tribunal's inherent power and Rule 77(A)(iv) and Rule 77(B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Beqaj, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a -- to enter a plea on these charges within 30 days after your initial appearance. However, you are entitled to enter a plea on this same day if you would prefer to do that. Would you like to use the 30 days to consider it or would you like to enter a plea today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have said it before, and I say today that I am not guilty. I have not been guilty. I have recorded in Pristina that you are arresting an innocent person and taking him to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Beqaj, I do understand your answer to be that you would like to enter a plea today. I will read to you each of the counts of the indictment which has been read in its entirety to you. Count 1 charges you with contempt of the Tribunal, punishable under this Tribunal's inherent power and Rule 77(A)(iv) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of this Tribunal. How do you plead on count 1? Could you please tell us how you plead, guilty or not guilty, on count 1. You do not receive translation at this moment I do understand. There seems to be a technical problem, Madam Registrar. You still cannot hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you now. I can hear you now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I put again the question to you. How do you plead on count 1, contempt of the Tribunal, punishable under this Tribunal's inherent power and Rule 77(A)(iv) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am innocent, and I have stated this many times. I'm innocent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think at this moment it's just sufficient to express whether you plead guilty or not guilty. I do understand your answer to be a not guilty plea, and therefore the Trial Chamber records the plea of not guilty on count 1. And in respect of count 2, attempted contempt of the Tribunal, punishable under this Tribunal's inherent power and Rule 77(A)(iv) and Rule 77(B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the Chamber records the plea of not guilty under count 2. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. In respect of count 3, incitement to contempt of the Tribunal, punishable under this Tribunal's inherent power and Rule 77(A)(iv) and Rule 77(B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Innocent, truly innocent, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber records your plea of not guilty on count 3. Mr. Beqaj, having entered a plea, it's now time to consider your present situation in the Detention Unit. I'd like to give an opportunity to you or to Defence counsel, if you would leave it to Defence counsel, to submit whatever he deems necessary in relation to your health situation. That could be done in private session, if needed. That's the first issue. And the second one is the detention, whether you should stay in detention in The Hague or whether you should be released, whether or not provisionally. Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Your Honour. With regard to the first matter that Your Honour raised about the health of Mr. Beqaj, there are no submissions we wish to make at this point. In respect of the question of provisional release, I have taken instructions on that matter, and it is inevitable that there will be an application for provisional release but not at this stage. It is at this point still awaited for the Prosecution to provide the supporting material as they're required to do in 30 days. I believe that translation is ongoing at the moment, and it is in light of receiving that material and further inquiries being made and having a better idea of what the time schedule of this relatively small case will be that an application will then be considered and made in the future. So there are no further submissions on that point at this stage. There is, however, a submission that we do wish to make in respect of the conditions of Mr. Beqaj's detention in The Hague at the moment. An order was made, a decision of the Deputy Registrar on the 5th of November --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, Your Honour, but can we go into private session on this because of the nature of the order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dixon, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. It's a minor but fairly important point and that is that the spelling of Mr. Beqaj's first name is incorrect in the indictment. It may just be because of different spellings from Albanian to English in translation matters. However, I did wish to point this out, that the last letter of his first name is in fact an A and not an E. I have spoken to my learned friend about this, and he has indicated that the indictment can be amended to that effect, and if there was such an application that there would be no objection so that his name is referred to correctly. He is certainly the person referred to in the indictment, but it is important that his name is spelled correctly for future proceedings. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Cayley, it's not in dispute that the accused before us is the person indicted but that his name needs to be -- the spelling of his name needs to be adjusted in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, you can make probably an immediate order since there is no dispute between the parties, under Rule 50 that the Prosecutor amend the indictment, and we can go ahead and do that and file an amended version with the name spelled correctly. I think that's probably the cleanest way of doing it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it, Mr. Cayley, that you have no other plans for amendments on the indictments, because then I'd rather take them together in order to avoid that we have a first, second, third, fourth, or fifth amended indictment. But is this the only thing that you have for the near future in mind, I could give an immediate order, an oral order. Let me just find the --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I think it's Rule 50(A)(i)(C).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 50(A)(i)(C). Thank you, Mr. Cayley. So the Prosecution has now orally made an application to amend the indictment to the extent that the first name of the accused, last letter will not be E with trema on it but an A. Mr. Dixon, there's no objection --

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: There's no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to this application. Therefore, I gave you as my oral decision that the Prosecutor may amend the indictment in the sense as I just said. The only question, but I think this is where Rule 50(A)(i)(C) makes this a decision of the Chamber. I take it this is of an technical nature such that I as a Pre-Trial Judge can take the decision and, therefore, you're allowed to amend the indictment accordingly, Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dixon, is there any further issue you'd like to submit at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Not at this moment. I'm grateful, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there anything the Prosecution would like to submit?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: No thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Beqaj, this concludes your initial appearance before this Tribunal. We will hear at a later stage as indicated from Mr. Dixon about whether or not your detention should be continued. At this moment, I order the continuation of your detention in the United Nations Detention Unit, and a written order will follow today to that extent so that it's all put on paper. So whether you will be released at a later stage is not something which is decided upon at this moment. Your counsel Mr. Dixon has indicated that at a later stage he will or might apply for your provisional release. We'll then hear what the reasons are. We'll then also hear what the position of the Prosecution is and then a decision will be taken at that time. We stand adjourned.
